methods.label: Square the given sum twice
methods.explanation:
Squaring the given sum produces the next even powers, with a simple middle term because \(a\cdot a^{-1}=1\). The original equation requires \(a\ne0\), so all reciprocal powers below are defined.

Using the perfect-square formula,
\[
16=(a+a^{-1})^2=a^2+2+a^{-2},
\]
so \(a^2+a^{-2}=14\). Squaring this new sum repeats the same useful pattern:
\[
196=(a^2+a^{-2})^2=a^4+2+a^{-4},
\]
since \(a^2a^{-2}=1\). Therefore
\[
a^4+a^{-4}=196-2=\boxed{194},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\). This calculation applies to every \(a\) satisfying the given equation.
